summary: SpaceX achieved a major milestone as its Starship rocket reached orbit for the first time during its 14th test flight, though the mission ended early. In civil space developments, NASA is increasing support for Boeing’s Starliner spacecraft—targeting an uncrewed flight no earlier than December followed by a crewed mission in 2028—even as Administrator Isaacman issued a new Planetary Protection Directive amid a greater than 50 percent cut to the agency's FY 2025 Planetary Research and Analysis funding. Internationally, scientists analyzing China's Chang'e-6 lunar samples identified a magnetic fossil, while Artemis Accords signatories prepare to convene on lunar debris management and emerging space support. On the military front, the U.S. Space Force and the Defense Innovation Unit teamed up to acquire commercial satellites for monitoring geostationary orbit, alongside major defense procurement news including Boeing winning the Navy’s next-generation F/A-XX fighter contract and RTX securing a $20.7 billion Pentagon deal for AMRAAM missiles. Looking ahead, observers should watch for Star Catcher’s upcoming orbital power-beaming demonstration, which is now ready for launch.
